solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: About to be able to pass round a brandy

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: turning round sends the words for able and pass back to front

parts.note: to be able is to be capable, so can
to pass a turn in a game is to go

explanation.surface: Someone who has the means offers to hand round a glass of brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns CANGO back to front, giving OGNAC after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a brandy distilled in the region around the French town of that name.

clue.text: Even locking artist in church is OK

indicators.note: locking means holding the artist fast inside the even word

parts.note: clean can mean smooth and even, as in a clean edge
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Even letting an artist work inside a church is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb but means CLEAN, smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission, an approval or go-ahead as when a flight is given the nod.

clue.text: Wrapped in silver, a pair of round cheeses? Just the one

indicators.note: round means the combined letters are turned about and read backwards
wrapped in means the pair sits inside the silver

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: A couple of round cheeses wrapped in silver foil, or perhaps just a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the one' makes the plural 'cheeses' singular; 'round' turns ADUOG back to front. 'round' looks like a description of the cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a single round Dutch cheese, named after the town where it was traded.

clue.text: Changeable Alastair, at heart a jerk

indicators.note: at heart takes the central four letters of the name, dropping two from each end

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A man called Alastair is fickle and, deep down, a bit of a jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of ALASTAIR is ASTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatic describes something unstable that does not stay in one position, so it shifts easily.

clue.text: Very good Australian criminal

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang something excellent is a real corker, a beauty
as in Jack the notorious Victorian murderer of Whitechapel

explanation.surface: An Aussie crook who is rather good at his job.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang uses the word for something excellent, and it also names a slashing murderer like Jack of Whitechapel.

clue.text: Tough guy possibly viewed as female?

definitions.text: Tough guy possibly viewed as female?

parts.words: Tough guy possibly viewed as female?
parts.note: a tough guy made of metal, whose female counterpart would be the Iron Lady or Iron Maiden

explanation.surface: A macho man who might be taken for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The female twist recalls the Iron Lady (Margaret Thatcher) and the Iron Maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a man of great physical toughness and endurance, as in triathlon events.

clue.text: Grimace cut short by bishop, one going after drug collection

indicators.note: going after means the following pieces come behind the drug

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to pout is to pull a sulky face
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bishop grimaces briefly as someone follows him after a drugs haul.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a miscellaneous mixture or medley, such as an anthology of assorted pieces.

clue.text: Legendary twin from southern Babylonia, from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue read from the south means from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Sumer was the region of southern Mesopotamia, in southern Babylonia

explanation.surface: A mythical twin hailing from the southern part of ancient Babylonia.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus's brother was the legendary twin, suckled by a she-wolf, who founded Rome with him.

clue.text: Maybe Norma's anxiety when brief lines replace service

indicators.note: replace means the lines take the place of the service letters

parts.note: consternation is anxiety or dismay
RN is the Royal Navy, an armed service
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL

explanation.surface: Someone called Norma worries when shortened lines take the place of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norma' looks like a woman's name; it is a small southern constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma, the Carpenter's Square, is a small star group in the southern sky, so an example.

clue.text: Maths relating to sun's motion, quite a feat, not half complex

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters are worked into a new order
not half means one half of the word feat is dropped, keeping its front pair

explanation.surface: Calculating how the sun moves across the sky is quite an achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' works twice: it ends the definition and joins QUITE, A and FE (feat less its second half, AT) as anagram fodder for 'complex'.
explanation.definitionFit: This astronomical formula gives the difference between apparent solar time and mean clock time as the sun's path varies.

clue.text: Without permission, away game needs colonial to be on time

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece being on another means it is written after it

parts.note: RU is rugby union
an ant lives in a colony, so it is a colonial insect

explanation.surface: A team missing an away fixture without leave, with a colonial player needing to turn up promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'to be on' a piece means following it. 'game needs colonial' is the whole of the part placed after time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil playing truant is absent from school without leave, which is exactly being away without permission.

clue.text: Call in mediator, initially to break apart wrestling Poles

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the wrestling and poles pieces, splitting them

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of mediator

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A mediator is called in to separate two Polish wrestlers locked together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people; it is the two magnetic poles N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A summons is an official call or order to appear, as before a court.

clue.text: Surround section of Mayfair club with unopened barrier

indicators.note: with here means the trimmed barrier holds the section inside it
unopened means the barrier word loses its first letter

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
a section cut from the letters spanning mayfaIR CLub

explanation.surface: Surround part of a smart Mayfair club with a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: IRCL runs across 'mayfaIR CLub'; ENCE (fence without its opening F) goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To encircle is to form a ring round something, which is to surround it.

clue.text: Barge in River Trent, one done up inside

indicators.note: inside means the last word sits within the rearranged letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: done, as in done over or messed up, means the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A barge sails into the River Trent with one fellow refurbished inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' rearranges the river, Trent and one into INTERRT; 'inside' puts the up within. 'Barge' is the verb, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in on a conversation is to cut into it rudely, breaking it off.

clue.text: Famous golfer's standard set by a woman — at last

parts.note: a norm is a standard

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of woman

explanation.surface: A celebrated golfer's usual score is matched, finally, by a female player.
explanation.walkthrough: Greg Norman is the Australian golfer known as the Great White Shark.
explanation.definitionFit: Greg Norman was a world number one golfer and twice won the Open Championship.

clue.text: Overwhelming influx of heroin hidden in a simple cover-up

indicators.note: hidden in means the drug is tucked inside the drape

parts.note: a valance is a plain drape that hides a bed base or curtain rail
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Heroin smuggled in under a plain disguise floods the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a sudden flood of letters or complaints overwhelms whoever receives them, like snow down a mountain.

clue.text: Conservative clubs welcoming odd couples in election team

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so the two Cs hold the pairs between them

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
split election into pairs EL EC TI ON and keep the first and third pairs

explanation.surface: Conservative clubs host odd pairings while preparing an election campaign team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd couples' is not odd letters but the 1st and 3rd of the two-letter pairs of 'election'.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is the Glasgow football club, a famous team in Scottish football.

clue.text: Clergyman about to commence embracing a god

indicators.note: embracing means holding the a inside
the about letter moves to begin the word, to commence it

parts.note: a rector is a clergyman in charge of a parish
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A clergyman is about to start worshipping a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the C of RECTOR to the front gives CRETOR, which takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creator is the maker of the world, a title for God.

clue.text: Possible west-coast crook dropping in, causing tears

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the big US west-coast city

indicators.note: dropping means the word in falls out of the crook

parts.note: a crook is a criminal

explanation.surface: A shady character from the West Coast drops by and leaves everyone weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' flags that an LA criminal is just one kind of crook.
explanation.definitionFit: The lacrimal glands produce tears, so the word describes what makes the eyes water.

clue.text: Caterpillar caught close to branch beside twig

parts.note: CAT is the brand name for Caterpillar, maker of earthmovers
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of branch

parts.note: on can mean beside, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: A caterpillar is grabbed near the end of a branch, next to a twig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twig' looks like a small branch but is the verb meaning understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for grasp or understand, the same sense as the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Wrong people caught in distress

indicators.note: caught in means the people are trapped inside the wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: Innocent people wrongly caught up in a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering or anguish, a strong synonym for distress.

clue.text: A sign that letter below should be read in a nosey way?

definitions.text: A sign that letter below should be read in a nosey way?

parts.words: A sign that letter below should be read in a nosey way?
parts.note: the wavy mark over a Spanish or Portuguese letter signals a nasal sound

explanation.surface: A notice saying the letter beneath it should be read by a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nosey' reads as prying; it means nasal, spoken through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy diacritic over n in Spanish or vowels in Portuguese marks a nasal sound.

clue.text: One intended to keep private safe?

definitions.text: One intended to keep private safe?

parts.words: One intended to keep private safe?
parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier, and this helmet protects his head

explanation.surface: Something designed to keep your secrets secure, like a locked box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' reads as secret; it is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's steel helmet was nicknamed after its metal, protecting troops of every rank.

clue.text: Like rich people, old bachelors stopping in US city

indicators.note: stopping in means staying inside the city

parts.note: NY is New York
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, so BB is two

explanation.surface: Wealthy elderly bachelors stay over in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobby is British slang for smart or upper-class, describing posh, wealthy people.

clue.text: Feeling trapped in boozy actors' public house locked inside

indicators.note: locked inside means the house letters are shut within the mixed letters
boozy means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Stuck in a pub full of drunken actors after the doors have been locked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public house' looks like one item, a pub; 'public' is fodder for 'boozy' and 'house' gives HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Claustrophobia is fear of enclosed spaces, so someone with it feels shut in.

clue.text: Without restraints serenity somehow intact

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
the outside letters of serenity act as its restraints and are taken away

explanation.surface: Unbound and calm, someone's composure has survived undamaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping S and Y leaves ERENIT, which 'somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entire is whole, with nothing missing, so it remains undamaged.

clue.text: Evil enemy introducing an unknown catalyst

indicators.note: introducing means bringing the unknown into the middle of the rearranged letters
evil means wicked or corrupt, so the letters are twisted into a new arrangement

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A wicked foe brings in an unknown agent to set things off.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are proteins that speed up chemical reactions in living things, acting as biological catalysts.
